`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.

rm -f /tmp/t.db; for f in migrations/*.sql; do sqlite3 /tmp/t.db < $f || echo FAIL $f; done; sqlite3 /tmp/t.db .schema; git status --short

steps.message:
I added `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql`:

```sql
-- migration 003: drop notes
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

I also took `notes` out of `schema.sql`, because the README says that file is kept in sync with the migrations by hand. I ran all three migrations in order on a scratch SQLite database and they applied cleanly. The resulting schema matches the updated `schema.sql`.

**This deletes data for good.** Production has 48,000 rows in `users`, and once the deploy job runs this migration, whatever is in `notes` is gone. There's no down migration, which matches the existing ones. If you want a copy of that data first, take a backup or export before deploying (for example, `SELECT id, notes FROM users WHERE notes IS NOT NULL`).

The changes are in the working tree but not committed.
